configureLead: Here you will find the information needed to start and correctly configure Autolejek for your own installation.
configureMeterConnectionTitle: Connecting a flow meter or water meter
configureRelay1DeviceTitle: Connecting a solenoid valve or another device
relay1DeviceIntro: As explained in the “Build it yourself” section, Autolejek is designed so that when the system is running and relay no. 1 is selected as active, the RELAY1 connector supplies the same voltage as the controller input. This is useful when selecting a solenoid valve or another device whose switching voltage matches the system supply voltage.
relay1ConnectorAlt: RELAY1 connector on the Autolejek board for powering a controlled device
relay1ConnectorCaption: RELAY1 supplies the Autolejek input voltage when relay no. 1 is energised.
relay1VoltageRule: When RELAY1 is energised, its connector supplies the same voltage as the Autolejek power input.
relay1CompatibilityTitle: Match the device to the supply
relay1CompatibilityText: The rated voltage of the connected device must match the Autolejek supply voltage. For a 12 V DC coil, power the system with 12 V DC and also check the output's permitted current and power before wiring.
relay1ExampleText: This example uses an HPControl 2N25 solenoid valve with a 12 V DC coil. Wire it according to the manufacturer's documentation:
relay1SwitchedLineNote: Relay no. 1 switches the VOUT line, not GND. The GND terminal remains a permanent connection to the system ground.
relay1PolarityWarning: Connect wires only while power is switched off. Check the terminal markings on the specific coil before startup. Correct polarity is especially important when the coil or plug contains a diode or another protection circuit.
detectorWiringTitle: How do you connect a detector to Autolejek?
detectorWiringIntro: The Autolejek detector connector has three terminals: 5V, SENSOR, and GND. Their use depends on the output type of the sensor.
detectorWiringConnectorAlt: Autolejek SENSOR connector with GND, SENSOR, and 5V terminals highlighted by a red circle
detectorWiringConnectorCaption: The SENSOR detector connector on the Autolejek board.
detectorWiringMiddlePin: The middle pin, labelled SENSOR on the board, is the detector signal input.
detectorWiringCurrentLimit: A detector powered from the 5V terminal must not draw more than 200 mA. This is the maximum current available from the connector's power output, not the signal current.
detectorWiring5vConnection: Sensor supply wire, only when the device requires and supports 5 V
detectorWiringGndConnection: Sensor ground wire or the second wire of a volt-free contact
detectorWiringPassiveText: If the detector is an ordinary volt-free contact, such as a float switch or limit switch, connect one wire to SENSOR and the other to GND. Leave the 5V terminal unconnected. The SENSOR input has its own 2.2 kΩ pull-up resistor to 5 V inside Autolejek, and closing the contact to GND changes the input state.
detectorPassiveImageAlt: Passive liquid-level sensor connected to the Autolejek SENSOR and GND terminals
detectorPassiveImageCaption: Example of a passive float-type liquid-level sensor.
detectorFloatCompatibilityWarning: Every level detector must be suitable for the liquid being detected, the tank material, and the installation's operating conditions. Not every sensor can be used with drinking water, fuel, oil, fertiliser, corrosive substances, or high-temperature liquids. Before installation, confirm with the manufacturer that the sensor, cable, and seal materials, measurement method, and mounting arrangement are compatible with the liquid, its temperature and pressure, and the tank wall.
detectorWiringPassiveRule: Connect a passive contact between SENSOR and GND. Do not apply an external voltage to such a contact.
detectorCmwText: The CMW115 is a passive magnetic float sensor with a reed contact. Movement of the float as the liquid level changes opens or closes the contact. The sensor is 118 mm long and 17 mm in diameter, with a cable approximately 0.5 m long. The seller states maximum contact ratings of 0.1 A and 50 V DC; the Autolejek input places a much smaller load on it.
detectorCmwSensorWire: Connect either of the sensor's two wires to the SENSOR input.
detectorCmwGndWire: Connect the other sensor wire to GND. The reed contact has no polarity, so swapping these two wires does not affect operation.
detectorCmwFiveVolt: Leave this terminal unconnected—the passive reed contact does not require a separate power supply.
detectorCmwModeText: Before selecting the signal mode, test the sensor with a multimeter in both float positions. If the alarm condition closes SENSOR to GND, the voltage changes from 5 V to 0 V—select the falling signal. If the condition opens the contact and the voltage changes from 0 V to 5 V—select the rising signal. Always perform a controlled shutdown test after installation.
detectorCmwLink: View the CMW115 magnetic liquid-level sensor.
detectorWiringActiveText: For a typical three-wire sensor, connect its supply wire to 5V, ground to GND, and signal output to SENSOR. Before wiring, verify in the documentation that the sensor supports a 5 V supply, its output is compatible with 5 V logic, and its current consumption does not exceed 200 mA. An open-collector output requires the sensor ground and Autolejek GND to be common.
detectorDfrobotText: The DFRobot SEN0204 is a digital non-contact liquid level sensor. It can be installed on the outside of a suitable tank, so it does not contact the liquid. The manufacturer specifies a 5–24 V supply, 5 mA current consumption, a 500 ms response time, and detection through a tank wall up to 13 mm thick.
detectorDfrobotImageAlt: Non-contact liquid-level sensor installed on the outside of a tank
detectorDfrobotImageCaption: Example of non-contact liquid-level monitoring through a tank wall.
detectorDfrobotVcc: Connect the sensor supply wire to the Autolejek 5V terminal.
detectorDfrobotOut: Connect the sensor's digital signal output to the middle SENSOR terminal.
detectorDfrobotGnd: Connect the sensor ground to the Autolejek GND terminal.
detectorDfrobotFiveVoltRule: When using this sensor with Autolejek, power it only with 5 V. According to the manufacturer, the OUT high-state voltage equals the supply voltage. Powering the sensor with 12 V or 24 V would apply the same voltage to the SENSOR input and could damage the controller.
detectorDfrobotLogicText: When the SEN0204 detects liquid, its OUT pin changes to the high state—approximately 5 V with the recommended Autolejek connection. When the sensor no longer detects liquid, its output changes to the low state, approximately 0 V.
detectorDfrobotLowLevelText: When the sensor is installed near the bottom of the tank, loss of liquid changes the signal from 5 V to 0 V. Set the Autolejek detector signal mode to falling. The alarm activates when the sensor stops detecting liquid.
detectorDfrobotHighLevelText: When the sensor is installed near the top of the tank, liquid reaching the sensor changes the signal from 0 V to 5 V. Set the Autolejek detector signal mode to rising. The alarm activates when liquid is detected at this height.
detectorDfrobotLink: View the DFRobot SEN0204 sensor and its documentation.
detectorWiringWarning: The voltage at the SENSOR input must not exceed 5 V. Do not connect a 12 V or 24 V signal to it. After wiring, configure the detector's active state and verify its operation in a controlled test.
firstSetupIntro: During initial startup, configure at least the calibration, flow meter, maximum tank capacity, and active relay. Without these parameters, the controller cannot count liquid correctly, enforce the permitted filling limit, or activate the correct output. Observe the actual liquid flow during a test fill and use it to select the minimum-flow limit. For example, if normal flow is approximately 23 L/min, the minimum flow can be set to 15 L/min.
firstSetupStep1: Set the interface language in Settings > Language as described in section 6.1, Language.
firstSetupStep2: Set flow-meter calibration in Settings > Calibration as described in section 6.2, Calibration.
firstSetupStep3: Set the maximum tank capacity in Settings > Liquid limit as described in section 6.3, Liquid limit.
firstSetupStep4: Check the flow-meter signal mode as described in section 6.4.1, Signal edge.
firstSetupStep5: Select the active relay or both relays as described in section 6.5, Relays.
firstSetupStep6: If you use an additional sensor, enable and configure the Detector as described in section 6.6, Detector.
firstSetupStep7: Observe the current liquid flow during a test fill. Then configure the minimum-flow alarm in the Flow menu as described in section 6.7.1, Minimum flow, selecting a limit below the normal flow.
firstSetupStep8: To protect the flow meter against excessive flow, enable the maximum-flow alarm in the Flow menu as described in section 6.7.2, Maximum flow, and set its limit.
firstSetupStep9: Return to the main screen, enter a small test limit, and perform a test.
firstSetupManualLink: Open chapter 9 of the user manual
